Take a small amount of desi ghee using a spatula and put it on a filter paper.
Then press the substance on the filter paper using another filter paper.
Take the filter paper and place it in front of the lighting candle and move it over the flame, the light will be partly visible only through the spot formed by the ghee.
The reason is that when fat or oil is placed on a sheet of paper, it diffracts light. The diffracted light can pass from one side of the paper to the other, giving a translucent spot.

Huble's reagent
Using another dropper, take a small quantity of cotton seed oil and add about 4 drops of it into the test tube. Shake the test tube well.
4 drops
Take a small quantity of Huble's reagent using a dropper.
Add about 3 drops of Huble's reagent into the test tube containing the mixture of chloroform and cotton seed oil.
The violet color of iodine in the Huble's reagent does not fade away, indicating that the cotton seed oil is less unsaturated.
3 drops
Take about 3ml of chloroform in a test tube using a dropper.
Using another dropper, take a small quantity of linseed oil and add about 4 drops into the test tube. Shake the test tube well.
Take a small quantity of Huble's reagent using a dropper.

Add about 3 drops of Huble's reagent into the test tube containing the mixture of chloroform and linseed oil. The violet color of iodine in the Huble's reagent fades away, indicating that linseed oil is more unsaturated.
